Notes:
Ends 12:00 PM.
From your sheet: NaRhee, Jun, and Ann.
BOOKED — confirmed, do not move.
Confirmed for 10:00, the first slot of the day, for three adults. Budget two hours and expect to use less. A Korean derm clinic runs this as a pipeline: a ten-to-fifteen-minute consult each, numbing cream applied as each consult ends and left on fifteen to twenty minutes, then three to ten minutes of actual laser or shave per mole. Because the numbing on patient one is working while patient two is being consulted, three people take far less than three times one person — realistically out around 11:30, not 13:00. What pushes it long is first-visit paperwork in a second language, anyone turning out to have more moles than expected, and three separate payments at the end. Placed on the last full day deliberately: doing it here means you carry no healing wound through twelve days of Seoul heat, sun, and markets, and it leaves Wednesday's water park genuinely usable instead of theoretically off-limits. The cost of the placement is that you leave the country roughly thirty hours later — fine for a routine shave or laser removal, and the thing to reconsider if the doctor wants to cut deeper.
